kept.title: Cross-session task IDs must be namespaced {session}/{id}
kept.summary: Native Claude Code task IDs are local to a session; any cross-session/workspace reference must be the namespaced key `{session-uuid}/{id}`. native-tasks.js unions all session task files into one workspace list keyed this way (deps are intra-session blockedBy, namespaced to the same session).

kept.title: native-tasks.js is the SOLE adapter for the undocumented on-disk task layout
kept.summary: The `~/.claude/tasks/{session}/{id}.json` layout (and the projects-dir encoding) is UNDOCUMENTED / internal to Claude Code. native-tasks.js is deliberately the single adapter for it — if a Claude Code version changes the format, only this file should need updating. Don't read those files anywhere else.

kept.title: mkcert is required because TLS validates the cert issuer, not localhost
kept.summary: A self-signed cert can't shortcut local HTTPS: TLS checks the issuer against the trust store regardless of locality, so `mkcert -install` (adds a locally-trusted CA) is mandatory to serve the daemon's /mcp over HTTPS. This is the only reason the setup wizard insists on mkcert over a hand-rolled cert.

kept.title: Daemon ports: HTTP 8787, HTTPS 8788; inline UI only via custom connector
kept.summary: Shipped defaults: PORT=8787 (dashboard/graph), HTTPS_PORT=8788 (/mcp over locally-trusted HTTPS). The HTTPS custom-connector path is the ONLY surface that renders inline MCP Apps UI in the desktop app — local stdio MCP servers do not render it; otherwise you fall back to the preview panel.

kept.title: The PreToolUse write-gate FAILS OPEN when the daemon is unreachable
kept.summary: orch-gate.js denies a Write/Edit/Bash-write ONLY on a definitive 'no claim for this session'; if the daemon is unreachable, or the hook itself throws, it allows the edit (fail-open by design — never brick edits). So the gate is a guardrail, not a hard security boundary against a down daemon.

kept.title: Gate enforces writes happen INSIDE the registered worktree, but can't verify task legitimacy
kept.summary: Once a task has a registered worktree, the gate denies writes outside that worktree path (use the path from branch_task). Honest limit: it checks for a claimed in_progress task + worktree existence, not status truth — a rubber-stamp claim still passes it.

kept.title: The self-learn planner is ADDITIVE-ONLY — it caused a runaway once
kept.summary: Hard rules born from a real runaway: the planner NEVER cancels/supersedes/replans an in-flight task (that's the user's call), NEVER duplicates an open task (suggest_links + dedup BEFORE TaskCreate), caps output at 1-3 initiatives, and STOPs rather than fabricate busywork — graph bloat is failure.

kept.title: A stuck optimization ESCALATES to a human, never self-drops or auto-replans
kept.summary: decideOptimize returns 'stuck' (→ request_guidance) when the last K rounds produced no real win (no winner, or guardrail regression). 'stuck' deliberately outranks the silent stop reasons (diminishing/budget) because a problem failing every round needs human judgement, not a quiet drop. The only human-in-loop path is escalate — NEVER auto-cancel/replan.

kept.title: Optimize-loop defaults: epsilon=0.01, diminishing_rounds(K)=3, fixed precedence
kept.summary: DEFAULTS = { epsilon: 0.01, diminishing_rounds: 3 }; mis-set (negative/NaN) knobs fall back to defaults so a bad knob can't silently disable the control. Decision precedence (first match wins): target-converged → stuck → diminishing-converged → budget → iterate.

kept.title: ORCH_WORKSPACE overrides cwd-as-workspace (dogfood-finding #1)
kept.summary: mcp-graph.js used to post process.cwd() as the daemon workspace on startup, so any process loading the orchestrator MCP (e.g. a headless agent in a git worktree) hijacked the GLOBAL workspace pointer — repointing the live graph and blinding agents to the real workspace's learnings. Now honors ORCH_WORKSPACE when set (else cwd).

kept.title: Bench PLUMBING under-counts the always-resident MCP schema tax
kept.summary: MCP tool-schema tokens are cached into the system prompt and amortized across the session, NOT attributable per-message. So PLUMBING captures only tool_use/tool_result round-trips and under-counts the always-resident schema overhead. Read NET as an upper bound on work-only cost and PLUMBING as a lower bound on true orchestration overhead.

kept.title: Bench WIN requires all four guards to PASS; METRIC=(H_off−H_on)×5 − C
kept.summary: The v4 benchmark decomposes each arm into W (real work=diffTokens), H (hardness=output−W), C (consult overhead=ON−OFF cache cost). A WIN needs all four guards: precondition H_off≥2×W_off, fairness both-solve≥0.8, margin METRIC>0 and >pooled stdev, corroboration W_on/W_off≤1.1. Any guard failing → NO-WIN.

kept.title: Cross-workspace ghost edges store on the CONSUMER, foreign status resolved lazily
kept.summary: A dependency on a node in another workspace is a 'ghost edge': it lives in the consumer's overlay (fromWorkspace set means the provider lives elsewhere), and the foreign status is resolved on demand (cached, cycle-guarded) rather than stored. Don't look for it in the provider's graph.

kept.title: Heartbeat-loop code work is hold-merge: completes as MERGE PENDING, never merges to main
kept.summary: Under the autonomous orch-loop, every spawned code task works in an isolated orch/attempt/<slug> worktree, commits there, and completes as 'MERGE PENDING' — it never edits the live checkout and never merges to main. The self-learn-judge picks a winner but (in hold-merge mode) does NOT merge; merge is a deliberate human/dispatcher step.

kept.title: /agent/done CASCADES to release the task an agent held (fixes phantom in_progress)
kept.summary: Agent liveness fix #11: /agent/done releases the in_progress task the agent held; a staleness sweep releases abandoned claims (kill/crash/idle/cross-session) before reading native and busts the agg cache so reverted status shows same-build; releaseClaim also reverts native status to keep write-through in sync.
